note: Representative values at room temperature (25 °C), selected from handbooks and data sheets. Values depend strongly on lot, process, crystal phase, orientation, temperature and frequency; measured or supplier values should replace them before design decisions. Units: k W/m·K, σ S/m, E GPa, α ppm/K, ρ g/cm³, cp J/kg·K. Dielectric values are representative of the 1 MHz–1 GHz range.

materials.name: Epoxy (EMC / underfill matrix)
materials.note: DGEBA cured with amine or phenolic hardener. α 50–70 ppm/K below Tg; tan δ 0.01–0.03 near 1 GHz. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: BT resin (bismaleimide-triazine)
materials.note: Estimated values for the unfilled substrate resin. Commercial laminates contain glass fibre and fillers and differ substantially. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: Polyimide (PI)
materials.note: In-plane α of films ranges from 3 to 40 ppm/K depending on stretching and orientation; an isotropic representative value is given. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: PBO (photosensitive RDL dielectric)
materials.note: k, ν and cp are estimates. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: BCB (benzocyclobutene)
materials.note: Redistribution-layer and wafer-bonding dielectric. cp is an estimate. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: SU-8 (epoxy photoresist)
materials.note: E ranges from 2 to 5 GPa depending on cure. tan δ and cp are estimates. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: Silicone (PDMS, TIM / gel matrix)
materials.note: E = 3 MPa and ν = 0.49 (nearly incompressible). The large stiffness contrast increases the iteration count of CTE and elastic analyses considerably. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: PPE/PPO (low-Dk substrate resin)
materials.note: Modified PPE. cp is an estimate. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: LCP (liquid crystal polymer)
materials.note: Strongly anisotropic depending on orientation. In-plane α of films is frequently matched to copper (17 ppm/K). Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: PTFE
materials.note: α changes abruptly near the 19 °C phase transition. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: PEEK
materials.note: Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: Parylene C (conformal coating)
materials.note: tan δ at 1 MHz. Moisture and glass-transition values are typical of the resin class (moisture at 85 °C / 85 % RH: diffusivity D_w, saturated uptake c_sat in wt %, swelling coefficient CME per mass fraction); grades differ by a factor of several, so enter the data-sheet values for a real material.

materials.name: SiO₂ (fused silica)
materials.note: Spherical filler for EMC and underfill; skeleton of porous low-k films and aerogels.

materials.name: Crystalline silica (quartz filler)
materials.note: Orientation-averaged values. Higher k than fused silica, but also a higher α.

materials.name: SiCOH (dense OSG low-k skeleton)
materials.note: Estimated, strongly process-dependent values (E 8–20 GPa). Porous low-k films are modelled as this skeleton plus a pore phase.

materials.name: Borosilicate glass (glass substrate)
materials.note: Glass core substrates and interposers.

materials.name: Al₂O₃ (alumina)
materials.note: α-Al₂O₃. Spherical filler powders range from 20 to 35 W/m·K depending on purity and phase.

materials.name: AlN (aluminium nitride)
materials.note: k is sensitive to oxygen impurities (140–285 W/m·K).

materials.name: h-BN (isotropic approximation)
materials.note: Platelet crystal with in-plane k of 300–400 and through-plane k of 2–5 W/m·K. Orientation-averaged screening value; orientation effects enter only through platelet shape and alignment.

materials.name: Si₃N₄ (silicon nitride)
materials.note: Sintered bulk. PECVD thin films have much lower values (k 1–3 W/m·K, E 150–250 GPa).

materials.name: MgO
materials.note: Hygroscopic; used as a surface-treated filler.

materials.name: ZnO
materials.note: Semiconducting filler; σ varies by orders of magnitude with doping and oxygen vacancies.

materials.name: BeO
materials.note: Handling is regulated because of dust toxicity.

materials.name: SiC
materials.note: Electrical conductivity varies by orders of magnitude with doping.

materials.name: Diamond
materials.note: Representative value for synthetic diamond powder (single crystals exceed 2000 W/m·K).

materials.name: TiO₂ (rutile)
materials.note: Orientation-averaged εr (c axis 170, a axis 86).

materials.name: BaTiO₃ (high-k filler)
materials.note: εr ranges from several hundred to 5000 depending on particle size and phase; sub-micron powders are considerably lower.

materials.name: ZrW₂O₈ (negative thermal expansion filler)
materials.note: α and E are literature values; k, εr, tan δ and cp are uncertain estimates.

materials.name: Si (polycrystalline, isotropic approximation)
materials.note: σ of intrinsic silicon; doping increases it by orders of magnitude. Single-crystal E ranges from 130 to 188 GPa with direction.

materials.name: Cu (copper)
materials.note: εr of metals is not meaningful and is set to 1; conductive fillers are treated through σ in dielectric analyses.

materials.name: Ag (silver)
materials.note: Matrix of sintered-silver die attach (with pores) or filler of conductive adhesives.

materials.name: W (tungsten)
materials.note: Via and plug metal.

materials.name: SAC305 solder
materials.note: Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu.

materials.name: Invar (Fe-36Ni, low expansion)
materials.note: Ferromagnetic, but μr is set to 1 for EMI purposes.

materials.name: Stainless steel 316L (sintered filters, chambers)
materials.note: Austenitic stainless steel, annealed. Permittivity is not meaningful for a metal and is set to 1. Sintered filter media reach 30–50 % porosity.

materials.name: MWCNT (intrinsic properties)
materials.note: Axial intrinsic values of a single tube. Contact resistance and tunnelling are not modelled, so composite thermal and electrical conductivities are strongly overestimated; the result is suitable for percolation assessment only.

materials.name: Graphite / GNP (orientation-averaged)
materials.note: Extreme anisotropy (in-plane k 1500–2000, through-plane k about 5 W/m·K). Intended for use with platelet shape and alignment.

materials.name: Carbon fibre (PAN, axial isotropic approximation)
materials.note: Axial values of T300-grade fibre. Transverse values differ strongly (E about 15 GPa, k 1–2 W/m·K, α about 10 ppm/K).

materials.name: Carbon black
materials.note: Representative aggregate values with large uncertainty (σ 1e2–1e4 S/m).

materials.name: Ni (magnetic metal filler)
materials.note: μr is a representative low-frequency initial permeability; it decreases sharply above several hundred MHz.

materials.name: Carbonyl iron powder (CIP)
materials.note: Microwave absorber filler. Insulating particle coatings reduce the composite σ considerably. μr is an estimate.

materials.name: Sendust (Fe-Si-Al flakes)
materials.note: Near-field magnetic shielding sheets. μr, k, E and α are estimates.

materials.name: NiZn ferrite
materials.note: Low-frequency μr; it decreases at high frequency according to the Snoek limit.

materials.name: MnZn ferrite
materials.note: Very high low-frequency εr with strong frequency dependence (estimated values).

materials.name: Air / pore (void)
materials.note: Gas conduction decreases strongly in pores below 100 nm (Knudsen effect). Treated as a phase without stiffness in mechanical analyses.

materials.name: Vacuum (evacuated pore)
materials.note: Knudsen limit of nanopores. Replaced by the contrast-limited value in conduction analyses.
